records.name: New York Institute of Technology-Manhattan Campus

records.name: Sage College of Albany
records.campusFate: The Albany campus continues; Sage College of Albany was formally merged with Russell Sage College and Sage Graduate School into a single Russell Sage College with campuses in Albany and Troy effective July 2020.

evidence.claim: The Sage Colleges (Russell Sage College, Sage College of Albany, Sage Graduate School) shared a common president and board; in March 2019 the board voted to merge them into one institution under the name Russell Sage College from fall 2020.
Russell Sage College, Sage College of Albany and Sage Graduate Schools united under the single name Russell Sage College, one college with two campuses in Albany and Troy, effective July 1, 2020.

records.notes: The 2010 IPEDS combination appears to be an administrative reporting consolidation under the common governance already in place; the formal legal merger came in 2020. records.name: Sage Colleges System Office

evidence.claim: The Sage Colleges were governed by a common president and board of trustees and were merged in 2019-2020 under the single name Russell Sage College; the page does not mention a separate system office.

records.notes: This was an administrative/system-office IPEDS record with no campus of its own; it appears to have been folded into Russell Sage College's reporting. Inferred from the shared-governance structure; no page directly addresses the system office record.

records.name: Southern Methodist College
records.campusFate: The college still operates from its Orangeburg campus (Adden Hall), primarily online, sharing the campus with the Southern Methodist Church and other ministries; it has sold and leased some buildings since 2016.

In March 2016 the college elected to become primarily an online college effective fall 2016, and began selling and leasing some of its buildings.
Describes the college in the present tense as a private four-year college in Orangeburg, SC, moved there onto the Adden estate.

records.notes: The college's site does not carry a dated status statement, so 'currently operating' rests on the 2026 copyright and active application links. The IPEDS exit probably reflects loss of eligibility or accreditation (site states it is non-accredited); that is inferred, not stated. Unknown which buildings were sold or leased and to whom.

records.name: Ashland University Dwight Schar College of Nursing

evidence.claim: Ashland University acquired MedCentral Health System's College of Nursing in Mansfield in 2010; the nursing program grew from a hospital diploma program begun in 1919 and students complete their last two years at the Mansfield campus.
Ashland University's site lists the Dwight Schar College of Nursing & Health Sciences Mansfield Campus at 1020 South Trimble Road, Mansfield, Ohio.

records.notes: Wikipedia gives conflicting opening dates for the Mansfield nursing building (August 2012 vs June 2014). The IPEDS record is named for the later name 'Dwight Schar College of Nursing'; the acquisition year (2010) matches the IPEDS exit year.

records.name: Baker College Corporate Services

evidence.claim: Baker College presents itself as one institution with multiple campuses under a single accreditation; the page does not mention a Corporate Services unit.

records.notes: This was an administrative/employer-training unit of Baker College listed separately in IPEDS and then combined into Baker College; no fetched page directly describes it, so 'not-a-closure' is inferred. records.name: Center for Psychological Studies
records.notes: No Wikipedia article (404) and two web searches turned up nothing establishing what happened to the Berkeley/Albany, CA Center for Psychological Studies. Only the IPEDS record (2007-2010) is available.

records.name: Corban University School of Ministry

records.notes: Inferred from the past-tense Wikipedia wording and the property listing; no page directly states the Tacoma campus closed, who bought it, or that the sale completed. The listing is linked to Northwest Baptist Seminary by the blog, but the seller (seminary or Corban) is not stated. A skillplum page lists the school at 4301 N Stevens, Tacoma. Only a pending sale is known, so buyerName/buyerSector/replacementSystem are left null. The 2010 merger date is the institutional merger, not a campus transfer, so transferDate is null.

records.name: Mary Lanning Memorial HealthCare School of Radiologic Technology
records.campusFate: The hospital-based school appears to continue in Hastings, Nebraska under Mary Lanning Healthcare.

records.notes: marylanning.org returned HTTP 403 to every fetch, so the school's own pages could not be opened. A web search snippet (not opened) described an operating program founded 1953, offering an AAS degree, JRCERT-accredited, with graduating classes in recent years; this is why still-operating is chosen, but the opened evidence is weak. The IPEDS exit likely reflects the program no longer being reported as a separate Title IV institution.

records.name: Mennonite Brethren Biblical Seminary
records.campusFate: The seminary continues on the Fresno Pacific University campus in southeast Fresno as Fresno Pacific University Biblical Seminary.

evidence.claim: The seminary, founded 1955 in Fresno, is now called Fresno Pacific University Biblical Seminary, 'formerly the Mennonite Brethren Biblical Seminary'; offers MDiv and MA degrees and is located on the Fresno Pacific University campus.
Fresno Pacific's seminary page presents an active seminary with programs and admissions.

records.notes: Renamed, not closed. The pages checked do not give the date of the renaming or of its integration into Fresno Pacific University, so transferDate is null.

records.name: New Covenant International University
records.notes: No Wikipedia article (404) and one web search found no institution of this name in Lake Worth, FL. A search result mentioned New Covenant University in St. Augustine, FL (formerly Destiny Christian College), but nothing connected it to the Lake Worth institution, so it was not used. Only the IPEDS record (2003-2010) is available.

records.name: Palmer College of Chiropractic-San Jose
records.campusFate: Palmer College's San Jose (West) campus operated as a branch of Palmer from 1980 and was phased out, ceasing operations in June 2025 when its leased building's lease expired.

evidence.claim: Palmer's March 2022 press release says the board voted to phase out the San Jose campus, which would cease operations in June 2025 when its building lease expires; students could finish at Palmer West through March 2025 or move to Davenport or Port Orange.

The San Jose campus opened in 1980 and 'closed in June 2025'; the board decided in March 2022 to phase it out citing lease costs, cost of living, the job market and the cost to deliver the program in California.

records.notes: The 2010 IPEDS exit was not a closure: the San Jose campus kept operating as a branch of Palmer College (Davenport, Iowa) until 2025, so the IPEDS drop appears to be a reclassification as a branch (inferred, not stated). The campus closed 15 years after the IPEDS exit. Palmer was a tenant, not the owner. Search results (not opened) suggested the building at 90 East Tasman Drive was listed for sale and a developer proposed housing there; an opened sfyimby page did not mention Palmer, so no buyer or reuse is claimed.

records.name: Richard Gilder Graduate School at the American Museum of Natural History
records.campusFate: The school continues to operate within the American Museum of Natural History in New York City.

evidence.claim: The museum launched the Richard Gilder Graduate School on October 23, 2006, accredited in 2009; it offers a PhD in Comparative Biology and a MAT in Earth Science, described in the present tense (MAT joined the school in 2015).

records.notes: The page describes the school in the present tense but gives no explicit 'operating today' statement. The museum's own page returned HTTP 403. The IPEDS record covers only 2010; why it stopped being listed is not established (the school remains a degree-granting unit of the museum).

records.name: Samra University of Oriental Medicine

evidence.claim: Refers in passing to the 'former Samra University of Oriental Medicine' where a person served as clinic director 2008-2010; implies it no longer operates but gives no closure date, reason, or successor.

records.notes: No Wikipedia article (404). One web search found no closure announcement or successor; older directory pages still list 1730 W. Olympic Blvd, Los Angeles. Likely closed or ceased around 2010-2011 but not established by a page that says so.

records.name: Silicon Valley University
records.campusFate: California regulators ordered the San Jose school shut in April 2018 after it lost ACICS accreditation; no source found on what became of its building(s).

evidence.claim: SVU lost ACICS accreditation at bachelor's and master's levels on Dec 7, 2017; on April 5, 2018 California regulators ordered it to close and refund students within 45 days.
KPIX/CBS report dated April 20, 2018 that state regulators shut the San Jose school, with classes cancelled and about 4,000 international students affected; says nothing about the facilities.

records.notes: IPEDS stopped listing it after 2010 although it operated until 2018, so the IPEDS drop does not mark the closure (it may have been listed under another unitid). Campus address and post-closure use not found; a web search turned up only unrelated Lundy Avenue property records.

records.name: Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary

records.notes: IPEDS drop in 2011 appears to be an administrative/record issue (the institution never closed); the specific reason was not established. swbts.edu returned 403, so only Wikipedia was used.

records.name: St Basil College
records.campusFate: The Ukrainian Catholic Eparchy of Stamford continues to operate St. Basil College Seminary at its Stamford, Connecticut campus.

evidence.claim: Seminary's own site describes St. Basil's College in the present tense, with college graduations through 2008 and events 'throughout the year' (footer 2022).
Article, recently updated, states the Eparchy operates the St. Basil College Seminary at 161 Glenbrook Road, Stamford; its seminary details date from 2005-2007 sources.

records.notes: No page with a 2025/2026 date confirmed current enrollment or operations; present-tense descriptions only. The IPEDS drop in 2011 is likely a reclassification of the small college seminary rather than a closure, but this was not verified. A separate St. Basil Preparatory School (1933-1990) is defunct and should not be confused with it.

records.name: St Petersburg Theological Seminary

evidence.claim: A Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the USA release says St. Petersburg Theological Seminary in St. Petersburg, Florida held its 25th commencement on May 16, 2010, with campuses in St. Petersburg, Tampa and Clearwater; it was operating in 2010 but this says nothing about later years.

records.notes: Wikipedia 'St. Petersburg Theological Seminary' redirects to the unrelated Russian academy. records.name: Sunbridge College

Sunbridge Institute's own site (2026 copyright, events through November 2026) shows it operating at 285 Hungry Hollow Road, Chestnut Ridge, NY, with teacher-education programs.

records.notes: IPEDS location is Spring Valley; the institute sits in Chestnut Ridge. Waldorf/anthroposophic teacher training was mapped to 'Eco / experimental college' as the nearest vocabulary term; 'Professional / career college' is an alternative.

records.name: Trine University-South Bend Regional Campus

evidence.claim: July 16, 2018: Trine's Education Center, in Mishawaka since 2008, is moving to a former Brown Mackie College building in South Bend and will continue to operate, offering associate's, bachelor's and master's programs.

records.notes: The IPEDS merge into 'Trine University-Regional/Non-Traditional Campuses' is inferred to be a reporting reorganization; no page was found describing it directly. Trine's Wikipedia article says its 1990s education centers were 'eventually moved to online' without naming sites, so the South Bend center's current (2026) status is not confirmed.

evidence.claim: Describes a distance-education school with a nine-building campus in Newburgh since 1981 that relocated to downtown Evansville in 2017, current mailing address PO Box 1107, Evansville.
The school's own site shows active enrollment, webinars scheduled through 2027 and a 2025 testimonial; it presents as a multi-denominational online Christian college and seminary.

records.notes: The IPEDS drop in 2011 coincides with its distance-education focus rather than closure. The fate of the former Newburgh campus (4233 Medwel Dr. in directory listings) was not established, so no buyer is recorded.

Valor Christian College's site (2026 footer, 2026 graduation) shows it operating since 1990 under founder Rod Parsley, ABHE-accredited and approved by the Ohio Department of Higher Education.

records.notes: Valor's own site does not mention the World Harvest name; the link between the two is from Wikipedia. The IPEDS drop in 2011 matches the January 2010 rename. The fate of the Wright Road building was not found, so no buyer is recorded.

records.name: Long Island College Hospital of Brooklyn School of Nursing

evidence.claim: July 24, 2011: LICH ended its nursing school and cancelled the incoming freshman class after its merger with SUNY Downstate, which is not authorized to award associate degrees in nursing.
Hospital stopped operating Aug 30, 2014; its property was later sold to NYU Langone (March 2020) after Fortis Property Group had planned a development there. Page does not mention the nursing school.

records.notes: The 2013 date comes from a search-result snippet of a Brooklyn Daily Eagle article (last class graduating May 23, 2013) that returned 403 when fetched, so it is not cited; the Brooklyn Paper page only establishes the 2011 wind-down. Buyer fields are left null because it was not established that the nursing school occupied a specific building later sold to NYU Langone; the hospital campus was split between Fortis and NYU Langone per Wikipedia.

records.name: Louisville Bible College

Describes the college, founded 1948, as current, listing a campus at 8211 Restoration Drive and president Kerry Allen (2020-present).

records.notes: The site does not mention accreditation; the IPEDS drop in 2012 is probably an administrative or reporting change (e.g., no longer Title IV participant) but this was not verified.

records.name: Darkei Noam Rabbinical College

records.notes: IPEDS exit in 2013 does not reflect a closure; the reason the record left IPEDS (reporting or Title IV change) was not established. The seminary's own site (dunwoodie.edu) returned 403 so only Wikipedia was used.

records.name: The College of Saints John Fisher & Thomas More

records.notes: Not a closure; IPEDS dropped the record in 2013 but the school kept operating. Reason for IPEDS exit not established (it is a law school not ABA-accredited, which may have affected federal reporting; this is an inference only).

evidence.claim: California College San Diego, owned by CEHE, was told to close Aug. 1, 2021 per CEHE's notice to the Department of Education; listed locations in San Diego and San Marcos.

records.notes: Duplicate IPEDS entry (unitid 478625, in IPEDS 2013-2014 with blank city, combined into California College San Diego). Same caveats as unitid 110945.

records.notes: The article gives no date for the repurposing and does not say whether the church previously owned the building or acquired it from the seminary; the church was presumably the seminary's sponsor, but that is inference. replacementSystem left null because no listed value fits church use of a seminary building.

records.name: CollegeAmerica-Colorado Springs South

evidence.claim: CollegeAmerica's Colorado Springs campus was one of six locations; all campuses were closed by the end of 2021 after the system stopped enrolling new students and lost accreditation at one campus in April 2021.
